article.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
article.description: Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time isn't stated: 'I have visited Paris.' Past Simple is used for finished actions at a specific, stated past time: 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Common mistake: using Present Perfect with a specific past time marker, e.g. 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect — should be Past Simple.
article.content: Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time isn't stated: 'I have visited Paris.' Past Simple is used for finished actions at a specific, stated past time: 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Common mistake: using Present Perfect with a specific past time marker, e.g. 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is incorrect — should be Past Simple.

Ever wondered when to say "I visited" versus "I have visited"? 🤔 It's simpler than you think!

Use **Present Perfect** (have/has + past participle) for actions connected to now or when the exact time isn't stated. For finished actions at a *specific* past time, choose **Past Simple**.

Remember: 'I have visited Paris' is great, but say 'I visited Paris in 2019' if you give a specific time!

Ye 'I have visited Paris in 2019' sunke kuch ajeeb laga na? Kyunki yeh galat hai!

Dekho, Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) tab use hota hai jab action ka connection present se ho, ya exact time mention na ho. For example, 'I have visited Paris.' Isme time specified nahi hai. Lekin Past Simple use karte hain jab action finished ho gaya ho aur uska ek specific past time bataya ho. Jaise, 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Yahan time ekdum clear hai. Isliye, 'I have visited Paris in 2019' incorrect hai. Kyunki 'in 2019' ek specific past time hai, aur uske saath sirf Past Simple!

Ab clear hua? Bottom line: agar exact past time bata rahe ho, toh Past Simple use karo. Jaise, 'I visited Paris in 2019.' Simple!

slides.body: Many English learners often confuse the Present Perfect and Past Simple tenses. The phrase 'I have visited Paris in 2019' is grammatically incorrect because the Present Perfect (have + past participle) is used for actions with a connection to now, or when the exact time is not stated. For finished actions at a specific, stated past time like 'in 2019', you must use the Past Simple. Therefore, the correct sentence would be 'I visited Paris in 2019'. Remember this key difference to speak more accurately!
